summary: Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) lookout near Celista, BC: a 2026 listing as likely standing, reached by a remote backcountry route with grizzly habitat.

facts.status_note: A 2026 guide lists it as the Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) Fire Lookout among lookouts confirmed or likely to have standing structures.

visit.trail_note: Walk of more than 11 km return from the 4WD sheep track to the meadows, or about 20 km return by mountain bike to Mobley Lookout; remote backcountry with grizzly habitat.

events.note: Rainlander guide lists the Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) Fire Lookout (Celista) among lookouts confirmed or likely to have standing structures.

evidence.supports: Firelookout.ca places the Crowfoot Fire Lookout in Columbia-Shuswap, BC
The Rainlander guide names the lookout Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) Fire Lookout, near Celista
The 2026 guide lists lookouts confirmed or likely to have standing structures
evidence.quote: The following lookouts are confirmed to have standing structures or are likely to still have unmaintained standing structures as of 2026.

evidence.supports: The trail route is historic and important to the Secwépemc communities
evidence.quote: This is an historic route important to the Secwépemc communities

evidence.supports: The route is managed in winter by the Crowfoot Snowmobile Club under Recreation Sites and Trails BC authorization
evidence.quote: Managed in the winter by the Crowfoot Snowmobile Club under authorization of Recreation Sites and Trails BC

evidence.supports: Walking and mountain-bike distances from the parking point to the meadows and to Mobley Lookout
evidence.quote: Park here for a walk up to the meadows and back (11+ km return), or a cross-country mountain bike ride up to Mobley Lookout and back (approx. 20 km return).

evidence.supports: The trail page warns of remote backcountry with grizzly habitat
evidence.quote: Be well prepared - this is remote backcountry with grizzly habitat.

evidence.supports: The route became an access route to the Big Bend Goldrush and served sheep herders and foresters
evidence.quote: that became an access route to the Big Bend Goldrush, sheep herders, foresters

evidence.supports: In summer the route is a hike or mountain-bike ride
evidence.quote: In the summer it makes an outstanding hike or mountain bike

evidence.supports: The parking point is at the 4WD sheep track
evidence.quote: junction with the 4WD Sheep Track at 11 km

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.ca and the brief use Crowfoot Fire Lookout. The 2026 guide uses Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) Fire Lookout, and the trail page uses Crowfoot Mountain and Mobley Lookout for the route. The story uses both names. The sources read do not say which summit carries the tower.

notes_for_editor: Confidence is low. No build date, staffing, fire history or tower description was found in the sources read. Searches returned no Crowfoot-specific history, and the Canada Lookouts BC index I read has no Crowfoot entry. The record's coordinates (51.087, -119.22194) sit about 13 km north-east of the coordinates printed on the trail page (50.98599403, -119.31795835), which may be a trailhead rather than the lookout. The record was not changed; please check the point. The brief's name Crowfoot Fire Lookout differs from the guide's Mobley (Crowfoot Mountain) name, and the story uses both. The trail page does not state whether the public may climb or enter the tower, so no access level is recorded. The Firelookout.ca page renders no lookout fields. No photos recorded.
